Richard Wagner. The revolutionary German composer, conductor, and theatre director who fundamentally transformed Western classical music and opera.

He is best known for his massive music dramas, most notably the four-opera cycle The Ring of the Nibelung, comprising Das Rheingold, Die Walküre, Siegfried, and Götterdämmerung. This monumental fifteen-hour cycle is based on Norse sagas and the Middle High German epic Nibelungenlied.

Wagner pioneered the concept of the Gesamtkunstwerk, or total work of art, which synthesizes music, poetry, drama, and visual arts into a single cohesive experience. He outlined this philosophical ideal in essays like The Art-Work of the Future and Opera and Drama.

Tristan und Isolde from 1865 is a landmark music drama famous for the Tristan chord, which appears in its opening measures with the notes F, B, D-sharp, and G-sharp. This chord avoids traditional resolution and is widely seen as the beginning of the breakdown of classical tonality.

His advanced use of chromaticism and leitmotifs pushed tonal music to its limits, paving the way for twentieth-century modernism. The leitmotif is the musical technique Wagner perfected, assigning specific melodic phrases to represent individual characters, objects like the Ring or the sword Nothung, or abstract concepts, which develop and intertwine throughout the drama.

Wagner designed and built his own opera house, the Bayreuth Festspielhaus in Bavaria, Germany. It was funded in part by King Ludwig II of Bavaria. The opera house features a hidden orchestra pit that blends the sound of the instruments with the singers' voices.

Ride of the Valkyries is the thunderous, brass-heavy prelude to Act III of Die Walküre, famously used in popular culture such as the helicopter scene in Apocalypse Now.

The Bridal Chorus, popularly known as Here Comes the Bride, is the wedding march from his 1850 romantic opera Lohengrin.

Parsifal from 1882 is his final completed music drama, centered on the Arthurian quest for the Holy Grail. He designated it as a sacred festival play and forbade it from being performed outside Bayreuth for thirty years.

Siegfried Idyll is a chamber symphonic poem composed as a surprise birthday gift for his second wife, Cosima, performed on the stairs of their villa at Tribschen.

Wagner remains one of the most controversial figures in cultural history. While his musical genius is undisputed, his aggressive German nationalism and virulent anti-Semitic writings, particularly his essay Jewishness in Music, have cast a dark shadow over his legacy. Decades after his death, his music was championed by Adolf Hitler and the Nazi regime, leading to an informal, ongoing ban on public performances of his works in Israel. He was the son-in-law of fellow composer Franz Liszt, having married Liszt's daughter Cosima. He represents the leading and most controversial figure of late nineteenth-century German Romanticism.
